decision.title: Indie Build vs Stay NYC
decision.question: Should I quit my job to build my own product full-time, or stay at my established company in New York at $165K?

path_a.label: Indie Build
path_a.notes: Quit job to build own product full-time with no stated pay

path_b.label: Stay NYC Company
path_b.notes: Stay at established company in New York

A.label: Indie Build
A.summary: In this simulated world, quitting gives full ownership and autonomy from day one. That fit is paid for with a short runway, and savings run out around months 12-14 without income, pushing freelance work and later re-employment into the story.
top_tradeoffs: more ownership and autonomy, less income stability
more broad learning from shipping alone, less team support and structure
more control over each day, less social contact and more money stress

comparison.summary: In these simulated worlds, Path A matches the stated priorities best on ownership and autonomy, both rated 5, but it puts the stated fear of running out of money on a 12-14 month clock. Path B protects stability and builds savings, which fits the stability rating of 3, but in this simulated world it leaves ownership and autonomy low for years. The core trade is not pay versus no pay alone; it is direct control now versus a larger buffer and a harder exit later.
dominant_assumptions: Path A assumes spending stays near $5,000/month and the product earns little or nothing in the first year.
Path B assumes pay continues with small raises and spending stays controlled enough for savings to grow.
Product demand, profession, and ease of re-hiring are unknown, and those unknowns drive most of the spread in Path A.
what_would_change_my_mind: Early proof of paying users or repeat use in Path A before savings get low.
Clear evidence the current role in Path B allows side building or a real internal ownership path.
A tested lower monthly spend, or a clear re-hiring path, that stretches or softens the Path A runway.

front_pages.headline: Seed-backed founder led small team on tight runway
front_pages.deck: In this simulated world, early traction brought a modest $75K salary and investor backing. Days were long but bounded, with thin savings of -$33K to $5K and 0-0.9 months runway.
front_pages.changed_because: In this simulated world, the early 1,000 users created support load that led to a small seed round, shifting the path from freelance plus product to seed-funded founder with a team.

front_pages.headline: Promoted contributor held steady role without ownership
front_pages.deck: In this simulated world, steady employment continued with about $175K pay. Savings held at $160K to $186K with familiar routine and ongoing commute strain.
front_pages.changed_because: In this simulated world, the shock did not reach this branch because there was no launched product at month 5 to gain users or raise a seed round.

verdict.why: In this simulated world, B kept steady pay and 26.5-37.7 months runway while A still had 0-0.9 months runway despite traction. B was untouched by the shock.
verdict.dominant_assumption: Early user traction converts into a closable small seed round.

comparison.summary: In these simulated worlds, Path A matches the stated priorities best on ownership and autonomy, both rated 5, but it puts the stated fear of running out of money on a 12-14 month clock. Path B protects stability and builds savings, which fits the stability rating of 3, but in this simulated world it leaves ownership and autonomy low for years. The core trade is not pay versus no pay alone; it is direct control now versus a larger buffer and a harder exit later.
dominant_assumptions: Path A assumes spending stays near $5,000/month and the product earns little or nothing in the first year.
Path B assumes pay continues with small raises and spending stays controlled enough for savings to grow.
Product demand, profession, and ease of re-hiring are unknown, and those unknowns drive most of the spread in Path A.
what_would_change_my_mind: Early proof of paying users or repeat use in Path A before savings get low.
Clear evidence the current role in Path B allows side building or a real internal ownership path.
A tested lower monthly spend, or a clear re-hiring path, that stretches or softens the Path A runway.
